text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The opposition Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) and Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) will appoint common representatives to run for senators in parliamentary elections later this year.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Over 700 firms from 21 countries are exhibiting at the international Salmed '97 medical equipment exhibition, the Interherba '97 herb products' fair and Domexpo '97 consumer goods fairs in Poznan, western Poland.

- Food prices inched up by 0.2 percent in the first 10 days of March compared with the previous 10 days, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said. Dairy product prices showed the highest growth, while the prices of meat, eggs and sugar declined in the period.

- Australia's Brewpole will invest up to $40 million in development of the Hevelius brewery in Gdansk and increase the capacity of a bottling line in the EB brewery in Elblag this year, the company said.

- A consortium formed by Finland's Lohia Rudus OYAB and Poland's Bosta Beton concrete maker will buy a 70 percent controlling stake in the OKSM minerals mine in Olsztyn, northeastern Poland, the economy ministry said. The mine's book value is 10 million zlotys.
- The private RP Telecom firm will provide telephones to 600,000 subscribers by 1999, it said.

- PZU, Poland's biggest insurance firm, will provide complete motor insurance packages for all new Opel cars sold by dealers in 1997, under an agreement signed with Opel's U.S. parent company General Motors.
- The listed Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy (WBK) has bought a stake of 500 B-series shares in the Commercial Union Poland insurance firm, nominally worth 1 million zlotys, WBK said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Poland's industrial output declined by 2.8 percent in February, though it was 8.7 percent higher than at the same time last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- Poland's insurance firms accumulated premiums worth 2.786 billion zlotys in 1996, which showed a 50 percent growth compared with 1995. The industry's combined net profit reached 109.9 million, showing a significant 71 percent growth over 1995 results, a survey by the Nowa Europa daily said.

- Vehicle dealers sold around 85,000 new passenger cars and 8,500 commercial vehicles in January and February this year, which showed a 34 percent and 40 percent growth respectively compared with the same period last year, a report by the Samar market monitoring agency said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Fiat Auto Poland is planning to employ 700 workers this year to develop production of the Siena model to be marketed in Poland and abroad, Fiat board director Enrico Pavoni said.
PARKIET
- The SFK cable maker's net profit will reach five million zlotys in 1997, showing a 200 percent upturn compared with the 1996 results, a report by IB Austria Securities said.

- The listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) will soon produce an I-series share issue worth up to 75 million zlotys to preserve its market position as a large part of its capital has been frozen through the purchase of a controlling stake in Bank Gdanski, BIG's spokesperson Wojciech Kaczorowski said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
